title: Healthy pods, unavailable service
brief: Users cannot reach the practice web service even though its workload appears healthy. Establish the impact, collect evidence, and repair service routing.
objective: Restore an HTTP response through the Service. Explain how its selector, pod labels, and endpoints connect, and cite your before/after commands.

title: Running does not mean ready
brief: A rollout has left the web service without ready backends. Investigate the readiness signal and restore service without removing the probe.
objective: Restore readiness and an HTTP response. Explain the failed probe and why disabling readiness would hide the problem.

title: The restarting application
brief: The practice application repeatedly exits after a configuration change. Use logs and workload configuration to identify and repair the failure.
objective: Restore a serving deployment. Explain the causal log evidence, the configuration correction, and how you verified recovery.

title: A workload with nowhere to run
brief: A web workload never becomes available. Determine whether it is waiting for scheduling or failing inside a container, then correct its placement requirement.
objective: Restore a scheduled, serving workload. Cite scheduler evidence and explain why restarting a container would not address this failure.

title: The missing web process
brief: A local practice web service is unreachable. Compare running containers with all containers and inspect the stopped workload before restoring it.
objective: Restore an HTTP response from the client container. Explain what container state and logs establish, and what they do not prove about root cause.

title: Two running containers cannot communicate
brief: The web and client containers exist, but their request path is broken. Inspect their network membership and restore the intended private connection.
objective: Restore an HTTP response from the client. Explain network membership, service naming, and why host port publishing is unnecessary here.

title: Connecting to the wrong listener
brief: The web process is running and the client is on its network, but the usual URL fails. Identify the actual listener and demonstrate a successful request.
objective: Run a successful client request to the actual port and explain the mismatch with the original URL. Cite logs and both request results; do not guess from a port number alone.
